attributes.action: Enforce Section 4 of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 on Factory Farms
attributes.additional_details: Section 4 of the Act makes it an offence to cause unnecessary suffering. Yet, this is completely bypassed by intensive farming. Millions of animals endure systemic suffering, crammed into barren sheds, unable to exhibit natural behaviors. The government accepts this extreme suffering as 'necessary' for cheap meat. With sustainable alternatives readily available, industrial cruelty is no longer legally justifiable. We urge the Government to close this loophole and strictly enforce the law.
attributes.background: Enforce Section 4 of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 in agriculture via statutory guidance. The Government must mandate that extreme confinement (e.g. farrowing crates), routine mutilations without anesthesia, and selective breeding for rapid, painful growth constitute "unnecessary suffering."
